value.account:
Two defects, both only reachable at targets >= 2.29 (rich loop values).
1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py (_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted): the 'may only override scalar' relpath check ran before the check for the compiler-generated exhausted-placeholder ref, so the generated `root.steps.<loop>__exhausted_placeholders.artifacts.result__report` ref for a path field in an inactive variant was rejected. I moved the generated-ref check first. It only passes when the validator option for generated refs is on and the ref equals exactly what the compiler recorded for that step/output, so authored YAML/relpath overrides (literal or ref) are still rejected.
2) After compile was fixed, execution still failed at 2.29+ for any union result with an on-exhausted state ref (even with no path field): at 2.29+ the match join reads result__* from the loop frame, where exhaustion stores an unresolved {"ref": ...} (at 2.28 the join read state__* directly), giving invalid_integer / unresolved discriminant. In orchestrator/workflow/executor.py _resolve_bound_address, a LoopOutputAddress value that is exactly the loop node's on_exhausted override ref is now chased with the existing _resolve_ref_value. Provider-produced dicts that merely look like refs are not resolved, so malformed provider output still fails.
Tests: new fixture tests/fixtures/workflow_lisp/valid/loop_recur_on_exhausted_union_path_variant.orc and a parametrized test (2.28/2.29/2.32) in tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur.py that compiles and executes to exhaustion; a negative loader test in tests/test_loader_validation.py that an authored ref override of a relpath output is still rejected. Ran test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, loops_exhaustion_state, generic_state_exhaustion, scoped_union_guards, and the exhaust-selected tests in test_loader_validation (all pass); the bugs/ program dry-runs clean at 2.32.
Considered/discarded: resolving refs in loops.py repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts (would change 2.28 loop artifacts, which an existing test asserts stay refs); resolving any {"ref"} in the structured join (would accept provider-supplied ref-shaped values); lowering the placeholder as a literal for 2.29+ (would diverge from the designed placeholder step).
Not covered: no real-provider run of the bugs/ program; the exhaustion path with a path field in the *exhausted* variant executed with a real file was not separately exercised; did not run the full suite.
value.summary: Allowed the compiler-generated exhausted-placeholder ref for relpath loop outputs in validation and made the runtime resolve exhaustion override refs in loop outputs, so 2.29-2.32 behave like 2.28.

value.account: Root cause (two layers). (1) orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py `_loop_on_exhausted_outputs`: from 2.29 (rich loop values) inactive-variant fields get an on_exhausted override {"ref": <placeholder step>}; for a relpath field the validator rejects any override ('may only override scalar repeat_until outputs'). Fix: skip the override for fields whose contract kind is relpath, leaving the loop-frame placeholder in place exactly as at 2.28. Validation is untouched. (2) After that, the exhausted run failed at runtime: the loop's on_exhausted scalar override `result__rounds` is stored as an unresolved {"ref": loop.artifacts.state__round} dict, and from 2.29 the typed join reads loop outputs via LoopOutputAddress, which does not follow ref payloads (the string-ref path used at 2.28 does). Fix in orchestrator/workflow/executor.py `_resolve_bound_address`: for LoopOutputAddress, if the artifact is a pure {"ref": str} payload, follow it with the existing `_resolve_ref_value`. Stored loop artifacts are unchanged. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_union_paths.py runs bugs/loop_result_paths/reviewed_change.orc end to end with a fake provider at 2.28/2.29/2.32: exhaustion yields UNRESOLVED rounds=3, approve yields READY with the report path, and a missing report file still fails the run. Related modules (loop_recur, generic_state_exhaustion, loops_exhaustion_state, rich_loop_values_e2e, scoped_union_guards, loop_state, at65) pass: 120 passed, 1 xfailed. Alternatives: first I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection in validation.py; this compiled but the runtime then stored an unresolved ref in a path artifact and failed, and it touched validation, so I reverted it. I also tried resolving own-frame refs when building the exhaustion artifacts in loops.py; that fixed the run but broke tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur.py::test_loop_recur_on_exhausted_scalar_frame_carriage_executes_through_shared_repeat_until, which asserts the stored ref, so I moved the resolution to the consumer side. Not covered: relpath fields nested inside optional/list/map (contract kind 'collection') are not special-cased; targets other than 2.28/2.29/2.32 were not run individually; the full test suite was not run; the validator still rejects relpath overrides by design.
value.summary: Loop results that are unions with path fields in non-exhausted variants now compile and run at 2.29-2.32 exactly as at 2.28, via a lowering fix and a runtime ref-following fix.

value.account: Two defects stacked. (1) Compile: at 2.29+ the lowering built an '__exhausted_placeholders' step and emitted an on_exhausted override {ref: placeholder} for inactive-variant non-scalar fields, including relpath ones; validation (unchanged) rejects any relpath on_exhausted override. At 2.28 those fields were simply not overridden and kept the loop frame's own placeholder literal. Fix in orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py (_exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values): exclude relpath-kind fields, so no placeholder step/override is emitted for them, as at 2.28. (2) Runtime: once it compiled, exhaustion still failed because the loop's exhausted artifacts kept compiler-emitted overrides as raw {ref: 'root.steps.<S>.artifacts.<K>'} dicts and the match join then validated the dict as an int/relpath (this also affected scalar-only union results at 2.29+, e.g. rounds). Fix in orchestrator/workflow/loops.py (repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts + _resolve_exhaustion_refs): at workflow version >=2.29, such refs are replaced by the value from the exhaustion frame snapshot (self loop) or a completed step's artifacts; unrecognised refs are left untouched; <=2.28 is not touched. Validation was not weakened (the relpath-override rejection and malformed-provider-output validation are unchanged). Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py runs the bug program end to end via run_workflow at 2.28, 2.29, 2.32 for exhaustion, approval (done path with a report path) and malformed provider output (path escaping the allowed root still fails the run). Related modules (loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, loops_exhaustion_state, strict_boolean_control_flow_e2e) pass. Considered and discarded: letting the validator accept relpath overrides when the ref is compiler-generated (it compiled, but runtime then failed on the unresolved ref and it loosens validation); resolving refs in the match join (wider blast radius). Not covered: resume of an exhausted run from a pre-fix state, other non-scalar ref overrides (lists/records) beyond what the existing tests exercise, and the full test suite (not run per instructions). Nothing committed; bugs/ untouched (removed the ignored .orchestrate dir my dry run created there).
value.summary: Loop results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants now compile and run at targets 2.29-2.32 exactly as at 2.28, via a lowering fix (no placeholder override for relpath fields) and a 2.29+ runtime fix that resolves compiler-emitted exhaustion refs.

value.account: Two compiler fixes in orchestrator/workflow_lisp/lowering/control_loops.py, both only for rich-loop targets (2.29+); 2.28 and earlier paths are untouched. (1) _exhausted_inactive_placeholder_values no longer materializes placeholders for relpath-contract fields, so on_exhausted does not emit a {ref} override for a path field in an inactive variant; the loop frame's own seeded placeholder (exactly what 2.28 relies on) is used, and the validator's 'may only override scalar repeat_until outputs' check is never tripped. (2) _loop_result_case_output_ref was disabled for rich targets, so the union result join read result__<field>, whose exhausted value is an unresolved {ref} dict that fails contract validation at runtime ('Output value is not a valid integer' for rounds). It is now enabled for all targets, guarded at rich targets by requiring the state field to be a flattened state field, so the join reads state__<field> as at 2.28. Found (2) only after (1) because compile-only checks pass before the runtime failure; both were needed for run-time parity. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py runs the bug's program (from bugs/) end to end through run_workflow at 2.28-2.32 with a stubbed provider, covering exhaustion (UNRESOLVED, rounds=3) and approval (READY with report path). Targeted modules (loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, scoped_union_guards, loops_exhaustion_state, strict_boolean_control_flow, session_artifact) pass: 200 passed. Considered and discarded: reordering the validator so generated refs bypass the relpath rejection (compiled, but the runtime then failed on the unresolved ref, and it touches validation); resolving {ref} override values in loops.py at exhaustion time (more general but changes persisted loop artifacts and runtime semantics for every rich target). Validation is unweakened: validation.py is unchanged, authored relpath overrides are still rejected, and malformed provider output handling is unchanged. Not covered: nested-record exhausted state fields whose path is not a flattened state field still go through the old rich path; other path-typed exhaustion shapes (path inside a record in an inactive variant, list-of-path) were not separately tested; loader_validation and human_input modules were not run; test_exhaustion expects the 2.28 value rounds=3 as the parity oracle, not independently derived.
value.summary: At 2.29-2.32 loop/recur results with path fields in non-exhausted union variants now compile and run identically to 2.28, via two lowering fixes (no relpath exhaustion placeholder overrides; union join reads state fields on exhaustion) with end-to-end regression tests.
